#### What this PR does / why we need it:
* fix the bug that if NodeIPs change, routes won't be updated
* add a UT
* refactor UT TestReconcile()

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
    Route controller should update routes with NodeIP changed
    When a node reboots or kubelet restarts, it is possible that
    its IP is changed. In this case, node route should be updated
    with the correct IP.
    In this PR, it checks if the IP in an existing route is the same
    as the actual one. If not, it marks it as "update" so the old
    route will be deleted and a new one will be created.
    There's a new field EnableNodeAddresses, which is a feature gate for
    specific cloud providers to enable after they update their cloud
    provider code for CreateRoute().

Fixes #98359

For the record, I don't think we've reached consensus in  SIG cloud provider either about whether this is correct. > Is this backward compat? what happens to route entries that was created prior to this update

Yes, the design is that if `TargetNodeAddresses` (new field) doesn't equal actual Node addresses, routes will be re-created.

Before the update, routes' `TargetNodeAddresses` is empty , which means re-creating is needed. One reason is that it is possible before the update, Node address change has happened. We don't have `TargetNodeAddresses` so we don't know. It is safer to re-create.

Agreed with Dan's comments above that we should have docs that outline what we expect to happen here. It seems like if kubelet detects a new address, it will update the node's status, but we don't necessarily expect all consumers of this status to react (e.g. Pods using host network would not be recreated to reflect the new address). Or maybe we should like this PR suggests but it's not documented? 

I think it would be helpful to open a separate PR that just updates the [node address API docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#nodestatus-v1-core) on what is expected when a kubelet starts to report a different address. Even if we're not proposing any changes and just documenting what is already happening.

Or maybe we should like this PR suggests but it's not documented?

But since Kubelet has updated node status, I still think we should fix the route for the node. or else, Pods running on this node would have routing issues. Could we update the docs separately while still get this PR merged?

review_comments: According to another comment, the rate limiter is tied to `maxConcurrentRouteCreations`. Do we want to share that for deletions, in which case should we rename it?  Is it configurable?
I didn't touch the rate limiter logic. Then, I think we should share that for deletion and rename it to `maxConcurrentRouteOperations`. It is not configurable and is hard-coded to 200.
It should be set true by specific cloud-providers when they import this new change and `CreateRoute()`.
Why is it a per-route setting?  Wouldn't it be set once for the route controller?

Do you suggest putting `EnableNodeAddresses` into `RouteController struct`? It seems reasonable.
Please correct me if I'm wrong. After a specifc cloud-provider updates the cloud-provider lib, if it set `EnableNodeAddresses` to be true, it will provide `TargetNodeAddresses` in `ListRoutes()`'s results. If it doesn't set `EnableNodeAddresses`, it won't provides `TargetNodeAddresses`. I think this is the expected behaviour of cloud-provider consumers.
Do we really need additional dep? Was that dep already there (used by something else)?
So we are only searching for `addrs0[0]`? we don't care about `addrs[1..]`? If so why do we nested loops?

If `found` is false, it returns false early. If `found` is true, then the outer loop will continue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f1dac70e53564762476f5e76b380032d15f019f7/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/route/route_controller.go#L429-L431
ah. it is equality not searching!. Thanks.
